newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU rules on how linear bonds affect state deficts.
newsitem.headline: EU rules on how linear bonds affect state deficts.

text.p: The European Union's statistics office ruled on Wednesday on how linear bonds, the financing of public infrastructure and state guarantees to export insurance affect national government deficits.
These are the latest decisions on how EU states must calculate the budget deficit, which is the key criteria for qualifying for the launch of the single currency in 1999.

On linear bonds -- bonds issued in several tranches from the same lineage --, the statistics office, Eurostat, said that for tranches issued beyond the 12 months after the first issue the difference between nominal value and issue price must be treated as interest.
This means tranches placed on the market with a price discount increase the budget deficit and issues with a price premium reduce it, Eurostat said.
Linear bonds exist particularly in countries where the financial markets are relatively thin, as in Belgium, Sweden, Finland and Portugal, it said.
Discounts and premiums on tranches issued during the first year must be treated as capital gains or losses without an impact on the deficit, it said.

On the financing and exploiting of public infrastructures, a problem which Eurostat said concerns particularly Britain, annual state payments to companies, after projects have been completed, represent the purchase of services and, therefore, increase the public deficit each year.
Payment of an initial investment grant and the acquisition by the state of the infrastructure at the end of the exploitation period have no budget impact, it said.
Finally, Eurostat said guarantees given by EU states to institutions specialising in export insurance affect deficits when exercised. -- Brussels newsroom 322 2876841
